## Proof

We show the limit equals 0 by bounding the numerator quadratically in $\|V\|_{op}$.

**Key bound on entries.** For any $n\times n$ matrix $V$ and any indices $i,j$, the $(i,j)$-entry satisfies
$$|V_{ij}| = |e_i^\top V e_j| \leq \|e_i\|\,\|V\|_{op}\,\|e_j\| = \|V\|_{op},$$
since $\|e_i\|=\|e_j\|=1$ for standard basis vectors.

**Expanding the trace.** By definition,
$$\operatorname{tr}(V^2) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} V_{ij}\,V_{ji}.$$
Taking absolute values and applying the entry bound above to each factor:
$$|\operatorname{tr}(V^2)| \leq \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} |V_{ij}|\,|V_{ji}| \leq \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} \|V\|_{op}\cdot\|V\|_{op} = n^2\,\|V\|_{op}^2.$$

**Forming the quotient.** For $V\neq 0$,
$$0 \;\leq\; \frac{|\operatorname{tr}(V^2)|}{\|V\|_{op}} \;\leq\; \frac{n^2\,\|V\|_{op}^2}{\|V\|_{op}} \;=\; n^2\,\|V\|_{op}.$$

**Taking the limit.** As $V\to \mathbf{0}^{n\times n}$, the operator norm $\|V\|_{op}\to 0$ (all norms on the finite-dimensional space of matrices are equivalent, and convergence to the zero matrix is equivalent to convergence in any norm). Therefore
$$\lim_{V\to \mathbf{0}^{n\times n}} n^2\,\|V\|_{op} = 0.$$

By the squeeze theorem,
$$\lim_{V\to \mathbf{0}^{n\times n}}\frac{|\operatorname{tr}(V^2)|}{\|V\|_{op}} = 0.$$

The limit is indeed equal to $0$. $\blacksquare$
